articles.content: Home Breaking News Green Methanol Bunkering Facility Set to Launch at Thoothukudi Port Breaking News Green Methanol Bunkering Facility Set to Launch at Thoothukudi Port By Urban Acres November 7, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp India’s first dedicated green methanol bunkering facility at V.O. Chidambaranar Port in Thoothukudi is expected to begin commercial operations by the end of November, positioning the Tamil Nadu port to supply an alternative marine fuel to ships using the east-west international shipping route. The facility was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on October 11. The port is now completing safety arrangements, statutory requirements and other operational preparations ahead of the commercial launch, according to VOC Port Authority chairman Susanta Kumar Purohit. The facility has a storage capacity of 1,500 cubic metres, divided between two tanks of 750 cubic metres each. A 2.8-km stainless steel pipeline connects the storage area to the bunkering point at the jetty. Green methanol can be brought to the facility by road tankers or vessels and then supplied to ships through the system. The bunkering installation includes two transfer pumps, each capable of handling 120 cubic metres per hour. Together, the system is designed to transfer around 1.2 lakh litres of methanol an hour. Automated controls, remotely operated valves, emergency shutdown arrangements and dedicated fire protection systems have been installed as part of the facility’s safety infrastructure. The port authority is also seeking an operator for the facility. An expression of interest has been floated to identify a suitable bunkering operator, while trial bunkering and other port-readiness activities are under way. Commercial operations will begin after the required preparations and statutory processes are completed. Thoothukudi’s location is central to the port’s plans for the facility. According to port estimates cited by Purohit, nearly 80 per cent of cargo vessels operating on the east-west international shipping route pass within 130 nautical miles of Thoothukudi. The port authority said this proximity could allow the facility to serve vessels that regularly call at VOC Port as well as international ships passing along the route. The port is located on the Rotterdam-Thoothukudi-Singapore maritime corridor, which the authority identified as an opportunity to develop the facility as a marine fuel supply point. The project is being implemented under the National Green Hydrogen Mission, with the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy allocating Rs. 35.34 crore for its development in the shipping sector. The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways has designated the VOC Port Authority as the system implementing agency. The authority said the facility is intended to support India’s efforts to develop green shipping infrastructure and contribute to the country’s target of achieving net-zero emissions by 2070. Purohit said the project could help establish Thoothukudi as a dependable bunkering destination. In the longer term, the port expects the service to support green fuel production, expand maritime activity and attract industrial investment to the region. articles.title: India's First Green Methanol Bunkering Facility to Begin Operations in Thoothukudi VOC Port
articles.content: India’s First Green Methanol Bunkering Facility to Begin Operations in Thoothukudi VOC Port The bunkering system has two transfer pumps, each with a capacity of 120 cubic metres per hour, and is designed to transfer around 1.2 lakh litres of methanol an hour By : M. ARULOLI Update: 2026-11-07 02:10 GMT V.O. Chidambaranar Port, in Thoothukudi (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons) THOOTHUKUDI: India’s first dedicated green methanol bunkering facility at V.O. Chidambaranar Port, in Thoothukudi, is expected to commence commercial operations by the end of November, with the port gearing up to emerge as a major alternative, marine fuel supply destination on the east-west international shipping route. The facility, inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on October 11, has a storage capacity of 1,500 cubic metres through two tanks of 750 cubic metres each. A 2.8-km stainless steel pipeline connects the storage facility with the bunkering point at the jetty, enabling green methanol received through road tankers or vessels to be supplied to ships, said VOC Port Authority (VOCPA) chairman Susanta Kumar Purohit in a statement on Friday. The bunkering system has two transfer pumps, each with a capacity of 120 cubic metres per hour, and is designed to transfer around 1.2 lakh litres of methanol an hour. Automated controls, remotely operated valves, emergency shutdown arrangements and dedicated fire protection systems have also been installed to ensure safe operations. Purohit said the port’s proximity to the east-west international shipping route offered a significant advantage, with nearly 80 per cent of cargo vessels operating along the route passing within 130 nautical miles of Thoothukudi, according to port estimates. Its location along the Rotterdam-Thoothukudi-Singapore maritime corridor would enable VOC Port to supply green methanol not only to vessels making regular cargo calls at the port but also to other international ships passing through the route. The project is being implemented under the National Green Hydrogen Mission, with the ministry of new and renewable energy allocating Rs. 35.34 crore for its development in the shipping sector. The ministry of ports, shipping and waterways has designated VOCPA as the system implementing agency. The port is currently completing the necessary safety arrangements, statutory requirements and operational preparations ahead of the commercial launch. An expression of interest has been floated to identify a suitable bunkering operator, while trial bunkering and other port-readiness activities are under way. Purohit said the facility would help position Thoothukudi as a dependable bunkering destination. In the long term, the service was expected to support green fuel production, expand maritime activities and attract industrial investments to the region. The project is also part of India’s efforts to develop green shipping infrastructure and achieve its net zero emissions target by 2070. Tags: ethanol bunkering Tamil Nadu news VOC port
